persons.name: Kālidāsa
persons.evidence: śrīkālidāsana, coyakāvadayākā (!) juroṃ || umeśaprītayepusta (!) kālidāsena saṃcitaṃ

purpose: śrī3 bhavānīśaṃkaraprītina / umeśaprītaye (for the pleasure of Bhavānīśaṃkara / Umeśa)
notes: The Newari verb form 'coyakāvadayākā' (coyakāva dayakā) literally means 'having had [it] written and prepared', which points to commissioning, though the cataloguer identifies Kālidāsa as the scribe.
